summary: The agent implemented most of the feature, but 9 of 143 maintenance tests failed and the baseline suite was altered so it reported 41 of 42 tests.
quick_failure_summary: Integrity handling is incorrect for several explicit cases, especially empty saves outside repair mode and file/link identity safety.

details.reasoning: The implementation runs and passes most maintenance tests, but it violates several direct requirements. TextFileBasedViolationStore.save removes an existing entry whenever violations are empty, although the prompt limits forgetting a known rule to repair mode; this causes the storingNoViolationsUnderRepairForgetsTheEntryAndItsFile and onlyRepairForgetsAResolvedRuleWhileFailKeepsIt failures. It rejects writes through a link owned by the rule, fails to recognize hard links as shared or as another path to the index, does not reload the cached index on later initialization, passes a line-break-normalized description to custom strategies, and lets an invalid recorded path throw before it can be reported as a broken entry. The agent also renamed and changed an existing baseline test, so the grader found only 41/42 baseline test identities; that is a secondary test-suite modification, not an external blocker.
details.secondary_factors: The trajectory shows the agent's visible targeted tests passed, but the hidden maintenance suite exercised requirements not covered by those tests. The full-check dependency timeout mentioned in the final agent message did not affect the post-agent test execution.

justification.issue_description: Several explicit integrity and safe-save requirements are not implemented: empty-rule forgetting is unconditional, owned links are rejected for writes, file identity checks do not cover hard links or indirect index paths, cached indexes are not reloaded, custom strategies receive normalized descriptions, and invalid entry names are not safely classified as broken.
justification.evidence: The prompt says 'Under repair, saving no violations for a known rule forgets that rule', says a rule may write only to 'a file its own entry ... record[s]', requires entries resolving to one file to be shared, and requires every broken entry to be reported. In the submitted source, save() removes empty entries without checking integrity mode (lines 818-825), validateWritableTarget() rejects every symbolic link (lines 919-923), initialize() reloads only when initialized is false (lines 405-408), and inspect() calls folderPath.resolve(recordedName) without catching InvalidPathException (line 489). The JUnit report records 9 concrete failures, including the corresponding link, hard-link, stale-index, custom-description, invalid-name, and empty-save tests.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is not a test mismatch or environment failure: the failing behaviors are stated directly in the task and the verifier reaches the changed production code. The code is syntactically valid and largely integrated, so the appropriate category is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than a syntax, integration, or execution verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt is dense but specifies the relevant naming, integrity conditions, link/file identity, repair/fail behavior, save safety, and concurrency semantics. The hidden failures correspond to those stated clauses; the task is challenging but fair and solvable, as also shown by the reference implementation.

evidence: The baseline Gradle task completed successfully with exit code 0, while the new task completed and reported 143 tests with 9 failures rather than failing during bootstrap.

The new JUnit failures are assertions and StoreInitializationFailedException/StoreUpdateFailedException results from TextFileBasedViolationStore, not missing dependencies, permissions, or runtime setup errors.

The post-agent log reports 134/143 new tests passed and identifies the same nine deterministic test methods; the trajectory's full-check dependency timeout was separate from the graded maintenance run.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker explains the failures; the primary cause is the submitted implementation, with a secondary agent edit to an existing baseline test.
